data.narrative:
ElectroFlow Technologies is a Seed-stage climate and energy company co-founded by Eric McShane and Evan Gardner that has raised $10M to date. The Climate & Energy sector includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, though narrow-stage peer comparables proved insufficient for robust benchmarking.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method given data constraints. Stage-Progression valuation applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $25M when applied to the $10M raised proxy. This method assumes ElectroFlow will progress along a standard capital formation trajectory. Peer-Median valuation was not applicable; while eight same-sector private companies exist (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix), filtering for same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints yielded fewer than three comparables, making median-based benchmarking unreliable.

The triangulated range is $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the Stage-Progression result given the single-method foundation. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage peer validation and the proxy nature of total-raised-to-valuation mapping. Obtaining traction metrics, customer revenue, or technology differentiation relative to the peer set would materially strengthen conviction in this valuation. Until closer peer data emerges, the $25M median should be treated as an estimate with material downside tail risk if Seed-stage capital economics in climate tech have tightened.
